I've been farming this land for 40 years. I know this soil, I know this weather, and I know what the neighbors do. At 70, I can't do everything myself — my son works in the city, my daughter-in-law too. I'll hire the machine station for plowing and harvesting like I've been doing the last several years. My back can't take it anymore.

The plan is the same as always: plant wheat in October after I clear the maize, harvest wheat in June, then get the maize in right away. I can't afford to rest the land — 7 mouths, and even with the off-farm income, the grain matters.

For wheat, I'll use the Jimai variety — everyone in the village is using it, it's reliable, and the county agricultural station pushed it years ago. It handles our dry winters okay with the well water. I'll irrigate at least 3 times: once before winter sets in to protect the roots from freezing, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading. Maybe a fourth if April is dry. I'll put down compound fertilizer and urea as base, then topdress in March. I'll spray herbicide in early winter and hit the aphids and powdery mildew before heading — that's what wiped out a neighbor's field a few years back, so I don't skip it.

For maize, I'll go hybrid — Zhengdan 958, it's what I know. Plant right after wheat harvest, no time to waste. Rotary till after wheat straw chopping from the combine. Base fertilizer down, then urea at jointing when the plant is knee-high. Two irrigations unless summer rains are good, then maybe just one. Spray for corn borer once. That's enough.

I'm not trying anything new this year. At 70, a bad experiment costs more than it's worth.
